Prealgebra · Lesson 10.4

Counting Pairs

Solve this lesson →All lessons

When order matters, multiply straight across. But when picking a pair, like two people shaking hands or two teammates, order doesn't matter, and a straight multiply counts every pair twice.

Problem
Six friends each shake hands once with every other friend. How many handshakes happen in all?
Show a hint
  • A handshake is a PAIR of friends, and the pair Ana with Ben is the same handshake as Ben with Ana, so the order does not matter. And everyone comes from the one group of six friends, not from two separate groups. So this is a pair count, where you will want to watch out for counting each handshake twice.
  • Set up the count the easy way first. Each of the 66 friends reaches out to the other 55 friends, so multiply to get 6×56×5. Now ask yourself the key question for pairs, did that count each handshake once, or did it sneak each one in twice?
  • You have 6×5=306×5=30, but every handshake got counted twice, once from each friend in the pair. So the honest count is half of 3030, and all that is left is to take that half.
Show the full solution
Each of the 66 friends shakes hands with the other 55, which gives 6×5=306×5=30. Every handshake got counted twice, once from each side, so take half and you get 1515​. The halving is what you owe whenever both people in the pair come from the same group. Ana with Ben and Ben with Ana are one handshake, not two.
Problem
In an 8-player round-robin tournament, every pair of players meets exactly once. How many matches are played?
Show a hint
  • Think about what one match really is. It is a pair of two players, and the match where Ana plays Ben is the same match as the one where Ben plays Ana, so order does not matter. And notice that both players come from the one group of 88, not from two separate groups.
  • Each of the 88 players could face any of the other 77, so multiply to get 8×78×7. Now ask the key question, since both players come from the same group, does counting this way count each match once or twice, and if it is twice then you will need to divide by 22.
  • You have 8×7=568×7=56, and every match got counted twice because each pair shows up from both players' points of view. So take half of 5656 and you are there.
Show the full solution
Each of the 88 players can face any of the other 77, which gives 8×7=568×7=56. Every match got counted twice, once from each player's side, so take half and you get 2828​ matches. Both players come from the same group of 88, which is exactly when the divide by 22 is needed.
Problem
44 students volunteer and exactly 22 work together each day. No pair repeats. How many days at most can be scheduled?
Show a hint
  • Two students working together is a PAIR, and the order does not matter, since Ana with Ben is the same team as Ben with Ana. And notice all four come from one single group of volunteers, not two separate groups.
  • Each student can be paired with the other 33, so reach for the multiplying habit and you get 4×34×3. But every pair gets counted twice that way, so think about whether you should divide by 22.
  • You have 4×3224×3​, which is 122212​. The most days is just how many different pairs there are, so finish the division.
Show the full solution
No pair repeats, so the most days you can schedule is just the number of different pairs. Each of the 44 students can partner with the other 33, which gives 4×3=124×3=12, and every pair got counted from both sides, so half of that is 66​.
Problem
An ice cream shop has 1111 flavors. A double scoop uses 22 different flavors, order doesn't matter. How many different double scoops are possible?
Show a hint
  • First decide what kind of count this is. You are choosing 22 flavors from one single list of 1111, and a scoop of chocolate on vanilla is the same scoop as vanilla on chocolate. So this is a pair where the order does not matter, and both flavors come from the same group, not two separate groups.
  • Set it up like a handshake. The first flavor has 1111 choices and the second has 1010 left, so a first pass gives 11×1011×10. But picking chocolate then vanilla and picking vanilla then chocolate land on the same double scoop, so each scoop got counted twice. That tells you whether to divide by 22 here.
  • You have 11×102211×10​ to finish. Work out the top first, then take half of it, and you have your count.
Show the full solution
The first flavor can be any of the 1111 and the second any of the 1010 left, which gives 11×10=11011×10=110. Chocolate then vanilla is the same dessert as vanilla then chocolate, so every scoop got counted twice and you take half, giving 5555​ double scoops.
Key idea
Count ordered, then halve. The number of unordered pairs from nn things is n(n−1)22n(n−1)​. Count the ordered pairs first, using the Multiplication Principle. There are nn choices for the first pick and n−1n−1 left for the second, giving n(n−1)n(n−1). Every pair is counted twice there, once as A then B and once as B then A, so divide by 22. A handshake, a round-robin match, a team of two, and a double scoop are all pairs chosen from one group of nn.
Problem
A dance class has 77 leaders and 66 followers. Every leader dances once with every follower. How many dances take place?
Show a hint
  • Before you count anything, ask what kind of pairing this is. A dance joins one leader with one follower. Are those two coming from the same group, where order would not matter, or are they coming from two different groups you can tell apart?
  • You are pulling one pick from the leaders and one pick from the followers, two separate groups, so multiply their sizes. Then pause and decide whether you need to divide by 22 the way you do when both picks come from one group.
  • Multiplying gives 7×67×6, and since a leader and a follower can never trade roles, no dance gets counted twice, so there is no dividing by 22 here. Just finish that one product.
Show the full solution
A dance takes one leader and one follower, two separate groups, so multiply the sizes and you get 7×6=427×6=42 dances, or 4242​. There is no dividing by 22 here. That fix is only for pairs pulled from one group, where the two picks can trade places.
Problem
At a party, 55 women shake hands with every other person, but the 44 men never shake hands with each other. How many handshakes take place?
Show a hint
  • A handshake is just a pair of people, and the order does not matter, since you shaking my hand is the same single handshake as me shaking yours. So really you are counting how many allowed pairs there are. Notice the pairs come in different kinds, some join two women, some join a woman and a man, and some would join two men.
  • Split the count into kinds of pairs. For two women, both come from the same group of 55, so that is a pair where you reach out and then divide by 22. For a woman and a man, the two picks come from different groups, so you just multiply the sizes and do not divide. For two men, none are allowed, so that kind adds nothing.
  • You should have woman-with-woman giving 5×4225×4​, woman-with-man giving 5×45×4, and man-with-man giving 00. Work each one out, then add the three counts together.
Show the full solution
Count the allowed handshakes by kind. Woman with woman draws both people from the same group of 55, so that is 5×42=1025×4​=10. Woman with man draws from two groups you can tell apart, so no halving, just 5×4=205×4=20. Man with man is not allowed, so 00. Adding the kinds gives 10+20=3010+20=30​. When some pairs are off limits, sorting into kinds and counting each with the rule that fits it keeps everything straight.
Key idea
One group or two, and what is not allowed. When both picks come from the same group, every pair is counted twice, so divide by 22 to get n(n−1)22n(n−1)​. When you pick one from each of two groups you can tell apart, the two picks cannot be swapped, so no pair is counted twice, and you multiply the sizes. When some pairs are not allowed, either count all pairs and subtract the forbidden ones, or split the pairs into types, count each type, and add.
Problem
A hexagon has 66 corners and 66 sides. How many diagonals does it have?
Show a hint
  • Every line in this picture joins two corners, so you are choosing a pair of corners where the order does not matter. All 66 corners come from one single hexagon, not two separate groups, so this is a pairs question and not a multiply-the-two-sizes question.
  • First count how many pairs of corners there are at all. Each of the 66 corners reaches out to the other 55, which gives 6×56×5, and then you divide by 22 because joining corner A to corner B is the same line as joining B to A.
  • Once you know there are 1515 pairs of corners in all, remember that some of those lines are sides, not diagonals. The hexagon has 66 sides, so take those away from the 1515 and you are left with just the diagonals.
Show the full solution
Each of the 66 corners reaches the other 55, which gives 6×5=306×5=30, and halving the double count leaves 1515 pairs of corners. Every pair is joined by either a side or a diagonal, and 66 of them are sides, so the diagonals are 15−6=915−6=9​.
Problem
A decagon has 1010 corners and 1010 sides. How many diagonals does it have?
Show a hint
  • Every diagonal joins two corners, and the order you name them in does not matter, so this is a pair where Ana to Ben is the same as Ben to Ana. And all the corners live in one single group, so you will count pairs from that one group rather than multiply two different sizes.
  • Count the pairs of corners first. Each of the 1010 corners can reach the other 99, which gives 10×910×9, and since each pair got counted twice you divide by 22. That total includes the sides though, so afterward you will need to take the sides back out.
  • You should have 10×92=45210×9​=45 pairs of corners. Now just remove the 1010 that are sides and not diagonals.
Show the full solution
Each of the 1010 corners reaches the other 99, and dividing by 22 for the double count gives 10×92=45210×9​=45 pairs of corners. Ten of those pairs are the sides, not diagonals, so take them out and you get 45−10=3545−10=35​.
Key idea
Diagonals of a polygon. A polygon with nn corners has n(n−1)2−n2n(n−1)​−n diagonals. Every line joining two corners is either a side or a diagonal, never both. There are n(n−1)22n(n−1)​ pairs of corners in all, and exactly nn of those pairs are sides, one per edge, so the rest are diagonals.
Problem
Six players each play every other player exactly 33 games. How many games are played in all?
Show a hint
  • First decide what you are really counting. A game is played by a pair of people, and the pair Ana with Ben is the same matchup as Ben with Ana, so order does not matter here. And the two players come from the same group of six, not two separate groups, which is the clue that this is a pair where you will need to undo a double count.
  • Count the pairs first. Each of the 66 people could face each of the other 55, which gives 6×56×5, but that counts every matchup twice since Ana with Ben and Ben with Ana are the same game, so divide by 22. Then think about what each pair does after that.
  • You have found that there are 6×52=1526×5​=15 pairs. Each pair plays 33 games, so the last step is to multiply 1515 by 33.
Show the full solution
Each of the 66 players faces the other 55, which gives 6×5=306×5=30, and halving the double count leaves 1515 matchups. Each matchup plays 33 games, so the season has 15×3=4515×3=45​ games. Count the pairs first, then multiply by how many times each pair does the thing.
Problem
A 17-player round-robin has 17×162=136217×16​=136 matches. Verify this by computing the sum 1+2+3+⋯+161+2+3+⋯+16 using the Gauss pairing shortcut. What is the value of this sum?
Show a hint
  • You are adding up the whole numbers from 11 all the way to 1616. This is the same total as the number of pairs you can choose from 1717 players, since order does not matter and Ana versus Ben is the same match as Ben versus Ana.
  • You could add straight across, but there is a faster way. Try folding the staircase in half. Pair the smallest term with the largest, then the next smallest with the next largest, and notice that every pair makes the same total.
  • Pairing the ends gives 1+16=171+16=17, 2+15=172+15=17, and so on down to 8+9=178+9=17. Count how many pairs of 1717 you have, then multiply.
Show the full solution
Pair the terms from the ends. 1+16=171+16=17, 2+15=172+15=17, and it keeps going inward to 8+9=178+9=17. The 1616 terms fold into 88 such pairs, so the sum is 8×17=1368×17=136​. That is the same 136136 as 17×162217×16​, because counting pairs from nn things is just adding 1+2+⋯+(n−1)1+2+⋯+(n−1).
Fun fact
The pair counts 1,3,6,10,15,…1,3,6,10,15,… are called triangular numbers because they equal the number of dots that tile a perfect triangle, 11 on top, then a row of 22, then 33, and so on.
Key idea
Repeats, and triangular numbers. When every pair does the same thing kk times, count the pairs with n(n−1)22n(n−1)​, then multiply by kk. The pair count also equals the sum 1+2+⋯+(n−1)1+2+⋯+(n−1), a triangular number. Add the people one at a time. The second makes 11 new pair, the third makes 22, and so on. So n(n−1)22n(n−1)​ and 1+2+⋯+(n−1)1+2+⋯+(n−1) are the same number written two ways, and you can add that sum quickly by pairing the ends.
Problem
A league has 1212 teams in two divisions of 66. Every team plays every division-mate twice and every team in the other division once. How many games are in the full season?
Show a hint
  • Sort the games into two kinds, the ones inside a division and the ones across the divisions. Inside a division, a game is a PAIR of teams from one group where order does not matter, so Ana versus Ben is the same game as Ben versus Ana. Across the divisions you are picking one team from each of two groups you can tell apart, which is a different kind of count.
  • For one division, first count the pairs with 6×5226×5​, then remember each pair plays twice, and there are two divisions. For the across games, you do not divide by 22, since the two teams come from groups you can tell apart, so just multiply the sizes 6×66×6.
  • One division gives 6×52=1526×5​=15 pairs, doubled is 3030, and two divisions make 6060. The across games are 6×6=366×6=36. Now add 6060 and 3636.
Show the full solution
Inside one division the number of pairs is 6×52=1526×5​=15, and each pair plays twice, so that division has 15×2=3015×2=30 games. Two divisions give 6060. Across the divisions you take one team from each, two groups you can tell apart, so multiply without halving, 6×6=366×6=36. Adding gives 60+36=9660+36=96​.
Problem
An icosahedron has 1212 vertices and 3030 edges. Each face is a triangle. How many interior diagonals does it have?
Show a hint
  • A segment just needs two corners, and swapping which corner you name first gives the same segment, so this is a pair where order does not matter, all coming from one group of 1212 vertices.
  • Start by counting every pair of vertices, multiply 1212 by 1111 and divide by 22 since each segment got named twice. Then think about which of those pairs you do not want, the ones that sit on a common face.
  • All pairs come to 12×112=66212×11​=66. Every face is a triangle, so the only pairs sharing a face are the 3030 edges. Now you just have 6666 and 3030 waiting to be combined.
Show the full solution
All the pairs of vertices come to 12×112=66.212×11​=66. Every face is a triangle, so the only pairs sharing a face are the 3030 edges. Removing those leaves 66−30=3666−30=36​ interior diagonals. A triangle has no diagonal of its own, which is why there are no face diagonals to subtract on top of the edges.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A 13-player round-robin has every pair playing exactly once. How many matches are played?
Show the solution
Each of the 1313 players faces the other 1212, which gives 13×12=15613×12=156. Every match got counted twice, once from each player's side, so take half and you get 7878​ matches.
Practice
Fourteen people each shake hands once with every other person. How many handshakes happen?
Show the solution
Each of the 1414 people shakes hands with the other 1313, which gives 14×1314×13. Every handshake got counted twice, once from each side, so halve it and you get 14×132=91,214×13​=91, or 9191​ handshakes.
Practice
A team of 1616 picks 22 players as co-captains (they share the same role). How many pairs of co-captains are possible?
Show the solution
The two co-captains share the same role, so naming one first does not make a new choice. Each of the 1616 players could pair with any of the other 1515, which gives 16×15=24016×15=240, and every pair got counted twice, so half of that is 120120​.
Practice
Eighteen points lie on a circle. A chord connects each pair of points. How many chords are drawn?
Show the solution
A chord is just a pair of points. Each of the 1818 points connects to the other 1717, which gives 18×17=30618×17=306, and every chord got counted from both ends, so take half and you get 153153​.
Practice
A pentagon has 55 corners and 55 sides. How many diagonals does it have?
Show the solution
Each of the 55 corners pairs with the other 44, and dividing by 22 for the double count gives 5×42=1025×4​=10 pairs of corners. Five of those pairs are the sides of the pentagon, not diagonals, so the diagonals are 10−5=510−5=5​.
Practice
An octagon has 88 corners and 88 sides. How many diagonals does it have?
Show the solution
Each of the 88 corners reaches the other 77, and halving the double count gives 8×72=2828×7​=28 pairs of corners. Eight of those segments are the sides of the octagon, so take them away and the diagonals are 28−8=2028−8=20​.
Practice
School A has 77 players and School B has 88. Every player from A plays every player from B once. How many games are played?
Show the solution
Each game takes one player from School A and one from School B, two groups you can tell apart, so multiply the sizes and you get 7×8=567×8=56​ games. Nothing gets counted twice here, so there is no dividing by 22. Halving is only for pairs drawn from a single group.
Practice
At a gathering of 66 women and 33 men, every woman shakes hands with every other person, but the men never shake hands with each other. How many handshakes happen?
Show the solution
Woman with woman is a pair from the one group of 66, so that count is 6×52=1526×5​=15. Woman with man takes one from each of two groups you can tell apart, so you just multiply, 6×3=186×3=18. The men never shake each other, so nothing more is added. Together that is 15+18=3315+18=33​.
Practice
A club has 66 players and every pair plays 44 games. How many games are played in all?
Show the solution
Each of the 66 players faces the other 55, and halving the double count gives 6×52=1526×5​=15 pairs. Each pair plays 44 games, so the club plays 15×4=6015×4=60​ games.
Practice
A league has 88 teams in two divisions of 44. Every team plays each division-mate twice and each team in the other division once. How many games are in the season?
Show the solution
Inside one division the number of pairs is 4×32=624×3​=6, and each pair meets twice, so that division has 6×2=126×2=12 games. Two divisions give 2424. Across the divisions you take one team from each, two groups you can tell apart, so multiply without halving, 4×4=164×4=16. Adding gives 24+16=4024+16=40​ games.
Practice
Find the sum 2+4+6+⋯+282+4+6+⋯+28 (the first 14 even numbers) using the Gauss pairing trick.
Show the solution
Pair the numbers from the ends. 2+28=302+28=30, then 4+26=304+26=30, then 6+24=306+24=30, and the total keeps coming out the same. The 1414 numbers fold into 77 pairs, so the sum is 7×30=2107×30=210​. Pairing the ends works on any evenly spaced list, since a step in from the left is matched by an equal step in from the right.
Practice
A cube has 88 vertices, 1212 edges, and 66 square faces (each with 22 face diagonals). How many interior diagonals does it have?
Show the solution
All the pairs of corners come to 8×72=28.28×7​=28. Of those, 1212 are edges and 6×2=126×2=12 are face diagonals lying flat on a face. What is left pierces the inside, so 28−12−12=428−12−12=4​ interior diagonals.
Practice
A pizza shop offers 2020 toppings. A 2-topping pizza uses two different toppings, order doesn't matter. How many different 2-topping pizzas are possible?
Show the solution
Each of the 2020 toppings can join with any of the other 1919, which gives 20×19=38020×19=380. Mushroom then onion is the same pizza as onion then mushroom, so every pizza got counted twice and you take half, giving 3802=1902380​=190​.
Practice
A heptagon has 77 corners and 77 sides. How many diagonals does it have?
Show the solution
Each of the 77 corners reaches the other 66, and halving the double count gives 7×62=2127×6​=21 pairs of corners. Seven of those lines are the sides of the heptagon, not diagonals, so 21−7=1421−7=14​.
